authoredSolutions.5: An electromagnetic wave is transverse: both \(\vec{E}\) and \(\vec{B}\) are perpendicular to the propagation direction (here \(y\)) and to each other. So the fields must lie in the \(x\)-\(z\) plane with \(\vec{E}\perp\vec{B}\): \(E_x,B_z\) or \(E_z,B_x\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.33: This is the Hoffmann bromamide degradation (amide + \(Br_2\)/\(NaOH\), i.e. hypobromite). In the basic medium the carbonyl carbon is expelled as carbonate ion, \(CO_3^{2-}\). Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.35: Hydroiodic acid cleaves the aryl methyl ether at the weaker \(O\text{-}CH_3\) (alkyl-oxygen) bond, not the strong aryl-oxygen bond. So 1-methoxynaphthalene gives 1-naphthol and iodomethane (\(CH_3I\)). Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.39: In \(CuSO_4\cdot5H_2O\), four water molecules are directly coordinated to \(Cu^{2+}\) (secondary valency = 4) and the fifth water is hydrogen-bonded to the sulfate ion. So the secondary valency is 4 and one water is hydrogen-bonded. Hence option (B).
authoredSolutions.41: Nitration of aniline with \(HNO_3/H_2SO_4\): partial protonation to the meta-directing anilinium ion together with the o,p-directing \(-NH_2\) gives mainly the para (C, ~51%) and meta (B, ~47%) isomers, with very little ortho (A, ~2%) due to steric hindrance. So the yield order is \(C>B>A\). Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.42: Colloidal \(CdS\) sol is negatively charged (adsorbs \(S^{2-}\)), whereas \(TiO_2\) sol is positively charged. So the charges are negative and positive respectively. Hence option (D).
authoredSolutions.44: Two molecules of cyclopentanone undergo base-catalysed (dil. \(NaOH\)) aldol addition to give the \(\beta\)-hydroxy ketone X; on warming with acid it dehydrates to the \(\alpha,\beta\)-unsaturated ketone Y (the aldol condensation product). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.46: Statement I is true: \(C_2H_5OH\) and \(AgCN\) can each furnish a nucleophile. Statement II (that \(KCN\) and \(AgCN\) give the same product) is false — \(KCN\) is largely ionic and attacks through carbon to give nitriles, while \(AgCN\) is covalent and attacks through nitrogen to give isocyanides. Hence option (A).
authoredSolutions.49: In \(CH_3\text{-}CH{=}CH\text{-}O\text{-}C_6H_5\): carbon a (the \(CH_3\)) is \(sp^3\); carbon b (the doubly-bonded \(=CH\)) is \(sp^2\); carbon c (the aromatic ring carbon) is \(sp^2\). So a, b, c are \(sp^3, sp^2, sp^2\). Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.76: \(ARB\) iff \(B=P^{-1}AP\) for some non-singular \(P\) (matrix similarity). It is reflexive (\(P=I\)), symmetric (\(B=P^{-1}AP\Rightarrow A=PBP^{-1}\)) and transitive (composing the similarity transforms). So \(R\) is an equivalence relation. Hence option (C).
authoredSolutions.79: The curve \(4y^2=x^2(4-x)(x-2)\) is real for \(2\le x\le4\), with \(y=\pm\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{(4-x)(x-2)}\). Since \((4-x)(x-2)=1-(x-3)^2\), the area \(=2\int_2^4\frac{x}{2}\sqrt{1-(x-3)^2}\,dx\); putting \(x-3=\sin\theta\) gives \(\int_{-\pi/2}^{\pi/2}(3+\sin\theta)\cos^2\theta\,d\theta=\frac{3\pi}{2}\). Hence option (C).

The roots of \(x^{2}+x+1=0\) are the complex cube roots of unity \(\omega,\omega^{2}\), which satisfy \(\omega^{3}=1\). Since \(x^{2}+x+1\) divides \(P(x)\), both roots make \(P\) vanish:
\[P(\omega)=f(\omega^{3})+\omega\,g(\omega^{3})=f(1)+\omega\,g(1)=0,\]
\[P(\omega^{2})=f(\omega^{6})+\omega^{2} g(\omega^{6})=f(1)+\omega^{2} g(1)=0.\]
Subtracting gives \((\omega-\omega^{2})g(1)=0\); as \(\omega\neq\omega^{2}\), we get \(g(1)=0\), and hence \(f(1)=0\). Therefore
\[P(1)=f(1)+1\cdot g(1)=0+0=0.\]
authoredSolutions.82:
For \(P=\begin{bmatrix}2&-1\\5&-3\end{bmatrix}\), \(\operatorname{tr}(P)=-1\) and \(\det(P)=-6+5=-1\). By Cayley\text{-}Hamilton, \(P^{2}-\operatorname{tr}(P)P+\det(P)I=0\Rightarrow P^{2}+P-I=0\), i.e. \(P^{2}=I-P\). Then
\[P^{3}=2P-I,\quad P^{4}=2I-3P,\quad P^{5}=5P-3I,\]
\[P^{6}=P\cdot P^{5}=5P^{2}-3P=5(I-P)-3P=5I-8P.\]
Hence \(P^{n}=5I-8P\) holds for \(n=6\).
authoredSolutions.84:
Using \(x+1=\left(x^{1/3}+1\right)\left(x^{2/3}-x^{1/3}+1\right)\), the first fraction is \(x^{1/3}+1\). Using \(x-1=\left(x^{1/2}-1\right)\left(x^{1/2}+1\right)\) and \(x-x^{1/2}=x^{1/2}\left(x^{1/2}-1\right)\), the second is \(1+x^{-1/2}\). So the bracket equals
\[\left(x^{1/3}+1\right)-\left(1+x^{-1/2}\right)=x^{1/3}-x^{-1/2}.\]
The general term of \(\left(x^{1/3}-x^{-1/2}\right)^{10}\) is \(\binom{10}{r}(-1)^{r}x^{\frac{10-r}{3}-\frac{r}{2}}\). Setting the exponent to \(0\): \(\frac{10-r}{3}=\frac{r}{2}\Rightarrow 20=5r\Rightarrow r=4\).
\[\text{Term}=\binom{10}{4}(-1)^{4}=210.\]

The critical points \(x=\pm 1\) are the roots of \(P'(x)\), so \(P'(x)=k(x-1)(x+1)=k(x^{2}-1)\), giving \(P(x)=k\left(\frac{x^{3}}{3}-x\right)+c\). The odd part integrates to \(0\), so
\[\int_{-1}^{1}P(x)\,dx=2c=18\Rightarrow c=9.\]
From \(P(-3)=0:\ k\left(-9+3\right)+9=0\Rightarrow -6k+9=0\Rightarrow k=\tfrac{3}{2}\). Thus \(P(x)=\tfrac{1}{2}x^{3}-\tfrac{3}{2}x+9\). The sum of coefficients is
\[P(1)=\tfrac{1}{2}-\tfrac{3}{2}+9=8.\]
authoredSolutions.86:
The segment joining a point and its mirror image is along the plane's normal \((2,-1,1)\). The displacement \((-3-1,\,5-3,\,2-a)=(-4,2,2-a)\) must be parallel to \((2,-1,1)\): \(\frac{-4}{2}=\frac{2}{-1}=\frac{2-a}{1}=-2\Rightarrow a=4\). The midpoint \(\left(-1,4,3\right)\) lies on the plane:
\[2(-1)-1(4)+1(3)-b=0\Rightarrow -3-b=0\Rightarrow b=-3.\]
Hence \(|a+b|=|4-3|=1.\)

Putting \(x=y=0\): \(f(0)=f(0)^{2}\). Since \(f(x)\neq 0\), \(f(0)=1\). By the definition of the derivative at \(0\),
\[f'(0)=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{f(h)-f(0)}{h}=\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{f(h)-1}{h}.\]
Therefore \(\displaystyle\lim_{h\to 0}\frac{1}{h}\left(f(h)-1\right)=f'(0)=3.\)

The plane contains the first line (direction \(d_{1}=(3,4,2)\)) and is parallel to \(d_{2}=(4,-3,7)\), so its normal is
\[\vec{n}=d_{1}\times d_{2}=(34,\,-13,\,-25).\]
It passes through \((1,-6,-5)\) on the first line:
\[34(x-1)-13(y+6)-25(z+5)=0\Rightarrow 34x-13y-25z-237=0.\]
Substituting \((1,-1,\alpha)\): \(34+13-25\alpha-237=0\Rightarrow -25\alpha=190\Rightarrow \alpha=-7.6\). Hence \(|5\alpha|=|{-38}|=38.\)
authoredSolutions.90:
Put \(y=vx\) (homogeneous). Then \(x\,dy-y\,dx=x^{2}\,dv\) and \(\sqrt{x^{2}-y^{2}}=x\sqrt{1-v^{2}}\) (as \(x\ge 1\)):
\[x^{2}\,dv=x\sqrt{1-v^{2}}\,dx\Rightarrow \frac{dv}{\sqrt{1-v^{2}}}=\frac{dx}{x}\Rightarrow \arcsin v=\ln x+C.\]
With \(y(1)=0\Rightarrow v=0\) at \(x=1\), \(C=0\), so \(y=x\sin(\ln x)\). The area is
\[\int_{1}^{e^{\pi}} x\sin(\ln x)\,dx=\int_{0}^{\pi} e^{2t}\sin t\,dt=\left[\frac{e^{2t}(2\sin t-\cos t)}{5}\right]_{0}^{\pi}=\frac{e^{2\pi}}{5}+\frac{1}{5}.\]
Thus \(\alpha=\tfrac{1}{5},\ \beta=\tfrac{1}{5}\), and \(10(\alpha+\beta)=10\cdot\tfrac{2}{5}=4.\)
